decisions.question: One canonical transcript schema
decisions.summary: Deterministic JSONL: one head record + N turn records, with a byte-span partition of the source that makes the round-trip gate arithmetic. All volatile provenance lives in a .decl.json sidecar, so the transcript file is a pure function of its source.

decisions.question: First family after Claude
decisions.summary: Accepted. The baseline's ANSWER is uncontested; its CRITERION is contested - substitute 'retire the widest fidelity gap first' for 'obvious next / biggest corpus'. Both converge on grok-tui here.
decisions.one_line_for_stage3: Decision (grok-tui) uncontested; criterion CONTESTED - order families by widest fidelity gap retired first, not by obviousness or corpus size. Read-only families first, live stores last.

decisions.question: crash-recover = check + restore-from-bak, OR a third writer
decisions.summary: crash-recover is a composition of existing verbs with exactly one mutation point (rebind). The suite has no code path that opens a vendor store for write, so 'never repair in place' is enforced by shape, not by policy.

rubric_additions.criterion: Fidelity must be provable, not asserted
rubric_additions.decides: Forces the byte-span partition. A normalized schema cannot satisfy the baseline's byte-identical round-trip gate.
All volatile provenance moves to the sidecar, so convert is idempotent and diff is a sha compare.

rubric_additions.criterion: Fences belong in the refusal taxonomy, not only in prose
rubric_additions.decides: WOULD_WRITE_SOURCE, CLOSED_VERB, NOT_MY_PEN as typed kinds. AGENT_BOUNDARIES.md item 14: a new session will not respect a social rule.

rubric_additions.criterion: Zero new writers, zero new clocks
rubric_additions.decides: Improvement is not bloat. Target met: no new authority, no new scheduled task.

gap_the_suite_owns.statement: COSMOS deliberately does not parse vendor transcript formats today.
gap_the_suite_owns.quote: The satellite never PARSES these files (the format is version-unstable) - existence + mtime is the whole signal.
gap_the_suite_owns.consequence: session-tools is the single quarantine for version-unstable vendor formats. Only the family adapters parse; the rest of COSMOS stays on existence+mtime. This is why the suite is a separate build, not a patch to cosmos_resession.

measured_blocker.finding: builds/cdeck is a submodule gitlink with no .gitmodules, so cosmos_recents_panel is absent from a clean clone.
evidence: cat .gitmodules -> No such file or directory
git submodule status -> fatal: no submodule mapping found in .gitmodules for path 'builds/cdeck'
measured_blocker.scope: Repo gap, NOT a runtime gap. Core :8770 is fine and Open Sessions is live on Keith's box.
measured_blocker.design_consequence: A session-tools test may not import cosmos_recents_panel at module scope. The migrate->recents assertion sits behind an availability probe, so the runtime-binding gate can still run in GitLab CI and on a peer's cold install.
measured_blocker.proposal: Either commit builds/cdeck/ as real files, or add a .gitmodules mapping. Not fixed by this run (P10).

d1_schema.name: cosmos-transcript/1
d1_schema.tail_rationale: Coverage proof lives in the sidecar - the house pattern (cosmos_validate.write_declared, cosmos_session.py:288-294).

why_jsonl: House idiom: authority ledger, sched ledger, and lease ledger are all JSONL.
Streaming: first corpus is 24.4 MB / 17439 turns; line-oriented makes diff a turn-indexed compare and check a single pass.
format_choice.why_not_sqlite: It would create a second store that could be mistaken for authority. Canon: large artifacts to a CAS, views are rebuildable projections, never authority (docs/FINAL_ARCHITECTURE.md:14). An index over .ctr.jsonl is welcome as a projection - GET /api/v1/recents already is that projection.

roundtrip.mechanism: The source byte stream is partitioned into ordered spans. Every byte belongs to exactly one span: a 'turn' span (carried by a turn record's src) or a 'frame' span (semantically empty bytes between turns - delimiters, headers, trailing newline - listed on the head as frames[]).
roundtrip.why: The gate becomes arithmetic a reviewer can check with a calculator, instead of a claim. That is the difference between a provable gate and a green log.

fidelity_modes.roundtrip_means: reconstruct from spans; exact and provable by the identity above
verbatim source preserved whole in the suite CAS by sha; round-trip is CAS.get(blob_sha); turn records carry src {blob_sha, key} where key is the row PK or filename

head_record.determinism_rationale: No timestamps, no tool version, no environment. That makes convert idempotent and diff a sha compare (A2).

fields.transcript_id: <family>-<native_id>, or <family>-<sha12(source_sha)> when the vendor has no id. Never minted (Open Sessions: no fake ids).
fields.native_id: str | null - the vendor's own id verbatim. null, never a substitute.
fields.cwd: str | null - the directory the session ran in. The Grok store's key, and the leftover-cwd crash signal.
fields.legal: bool - when true the body is NOT materialized from this profile (R7).
fields.sources: list of {idx, path, kind: jsonl|md|sqlite|dir, len, sha256, mtime, fidelity: span|blob, blob_sha?}. A list because Cowork = md + catalog row, opencode = db rows.
fields.frames: list of {after_seq, off, len} - span mode only.
fields.models: list[str] - distinct models that ACTUALLY answered. The runtime-binding value.
fields.t_first: float | null - null when the source has no timestamp. Never inferred.

fields.seq: int - 1-based, monotonic, gapless. A gap is UNPARSEABLE.
fields.t: float | null - epoch. null, never guessed.
fields.utc_off: int | null - matches the ledger's t/utc_off pair.
fields.text: str | null - normalized plain text; null for non-text turns.
fields.model: str | null - the model that answered this turn.
fields.parts: list of {type: image|file|tool_json|audio, sha256, len, mime} - a CAS pointer, never an inline blob.
fields.src: span: {source_idx, off, len, sha256} | blob: {source_idx, blob_sha, key}
fields.redactions: int - 0 unless this is an anonymize output.

turn_record.closed_role_enum_rationale: A closed role enum is what makes diff meaningful across families: a Claude tool_use and a Grok tool call land on the same role, so a cross-family diff compares conversations rather than vendor spellings. An unmappable source role is SCHEMA_UNKNOWN, never silently folded into meta.

sidecar.body_sha: sha over the turn records only. Survives a head-only change; the axis diff uses.
sidecar.tree_id: provenance stamp, NOT a gate. A transcript is a portable artifact and must open on a peer's cold machine. Contrast SEED.json, which is install-bound and refuses on mismatch.

hmac.rationale: SEED carries an HMAC because carry-over must be authenticated against THIS install's key (cosmos_session.py:108-116). A transcript must travel, and the suite must not touch install_key.bin - which the backup clock also explicitly declines to copy (cosmos_backup_clock.py:190-193). sha256 gives integrity; an HMAC would buy authenticity at the cost of portability and a key handle the suite has no business holding.

reasons_for.claim: The only non-Claude family with an in-tree, already-measured path resolver.
reasons_for.evidence: transcript_path('grok', cwd, sid, home) -> ~/.grok/sessions/<url-quoted cwd>/, bound to docs/research/AUTO_RESESSION.md 1.3/2.1
reasons_for.note: Every other candidate is UNMEASURED (Claude Desktop, per the baseline's own table) or not a chat store (Cursor cloud jobs, SGH work_orders/drop). Choosing an unmeasured store first would violate UNKNOWN-not-guess.

reasons_for.claim: RAILS = ('grok',) - the resession satellite already spawns and tracks exactly this family.
reasons_for.note: Its transcripts are the record of COSMOS's own construction - the corpus where a dropped turn is a governance loss.

reasons_for.claim: Converter-risk retirement: grok-tui is the pick that proves the schema generalizes.
reasons_for.detail: Claude Code is a single .jsonl per session - the easy case. A schema validated only against it silently bakes in 'one session = one file' and 'source is one byte stream'. Grok TUI is a directory keyed by url-quoted cwd with id-keyed entries inside: it forces sources[] to genuinely be a list, forces the span/blob split to exist before anything depends on it, and forces cwd to be a first-class head field - which is also the leftover-cwd crash signal the baseline names (SESSION_TOOLS.md:52, GFO gentle-falcon).

d3_crash_recover.shape_statement: crash-recover is not a new mutating verb. It is a composition of verbs that already exist, with exactly one mutation point - rebind. There is no code path in the suite that opens a damaged store for write.

steps.action: COPY (never move, never unlink) the damaged store to backups/session-tools/<stamp>/ via Backup.run(src, target), which already hash-verifies and writes _MANIFEST.sha256.json
steps.note: never-delete satisfied by construction, not by remembering to

steps.action: convert the READABLE PREFIX of the damaged store into a NEW .ctr.jsonl at a NEW path. Truncated sqlite opened file:...?mode=ro&immutable=1. Torn JSONL stops at the first unparseable line and records truncated_at_line.
steps.binding: discipline copied from cosmos/cosmos_lock.py:295-297 (a torn ledger must never read as free)

steps.action: when a *.bak_* or backups/verified/<stamp>/ copy exists, diff the backup against the damaged store and report the turn delta. The restore TARGET is a new path - never the damaged one.
the single mutation: point the vendor app at the recovered store

third_writer_fair_hearing.case_for: cosmos_lock.Arbiter is a real lease arbiter with monotonic fencing tokens and a four-phase fenced commit that never holds the OS mutex across the callback: Phase A reserves under the lock, Phase B stages unlocked with the token in hand, Phase C retakes the lock, CASes the token against the live projection, and only then os.replace()s. Stale tokens are REJECTED and ledgered. A third writer could acquire('opencode.db'), stage a repaired database, and install it under a re-verified token. Among COSMOS writers that is genuinely safe.

rejection.reason: A fencing token only fences participants.
rejection.detail: OpenWork/opencode and the Grok TUI never call acquire(). They are foreign processes holding their own file handles, and the arbiter has no way to make them present a token. So the fence is absent against precisely the writer most likely to be mid-write during a crash - the vendor app itself. Worse, Phase C's os.replace() would swap a file out from under a live vendor handle: on Windows that either fails outright or leaves the app writing to an orphaned inode, so the app's next flush silently reverts or re-corrupts the repair. A lease is a contract, and you cannot enter one unilaterally on another process's behalf.

rejection.reason: It would make the suite an authority, violating R6 (suite is tools; does not write ledger/kernel/sched) and the ratified single-authority rule.

The BTS two-writer deletion scar is this exact failure with a cost already paid (AGENT_BOUNDARIES.md item 9). Rebuilding the mechanism that caused it, with a fence that does not reach the other writer, is not a new idea.

seed_and_bucm_corollary.behavior: A bad SEED MAC, a missing SEED.decl.json, or a leftover running_session_file.toml produces a typed REFUSE plus a P10 proposal object for CCr. The suite never writes SEED.
seed_and_bucm_corollary.reuse: cosmos_resession.precheck_seed(seed_path, decl_path, live_tree_id) - already read-only, already structural - rather than re-implementing the HMAC check and risking a second, drifting verifier.

suite_cas.note: Same class, a SEPARATE store root, so Core's ledger CAS is untouched. cosmos_segments.py:344-346 takes an arbitrary root and has no ledger dependency.

family_adapter_contract.rationale: Four functions, so a new family is a file, not a refactor.
surface: discover(home: Path, hints: dict) -> list[SourceRef]   # read-only. never writes.
probe(src: SourceRef) -> dict                          # cheap identity: family, native_id, n_turns_est, fidelity
read(src: SourceRef) -> Iterator[RawTurn]              # ordered. yields a byte span or a blob key.
family_adapter_contract.write_prohibition: Neither discover nor read may write. WOULD_WRITE_SOURCE guards it.

refusals.shape: (kind, detail) with a .kind attribute and '[kind] detail' message - the house pattern, so cosmos_refusals.survey() picks it up with no change to the surveyor.

kinds.fires_when: no store found. NOT an error at scan - a legal, reportable fact.
present but the OS refused it
parses as bytes, not as this family (includes a seq gap)
truncated store. Refuse; never read as free.
declared span, measured blob (or vice versa)
span sum or sha does not reproduce the source
a source role/field with no canonical mapping. Never silently folded into meta.
tree_id mismatch where identity is actually required
a legal row requested from this profile. Refuse; do not open (R7).
GUARD: an adapter opened a source for write. The D3 fence, in code.
666 re-ingest, or 666 rebind. Both CLOSED by Keith.
asked to write the COSMOS live tree. P10, in code.

refusals.last_three_rationale: A3 - a future session that never reads this document still hits a typed wall. Prose fences drift; refusal kinds do not.

cli.root_rationale: --root is required and never guessed - same stance as Open_sessions.py:76 ('--root is required (no guessed live path)').
cli.dry_run: crash-recover --plan writes nothing and is how it should be run first, every time.

verbs.gate: count + absolute paths + per-source sha256 and mtime of stores that exist. '0 found' is a FACT, reported, not a failure.
n_turns + head sha. An absent timestamp stays null.

verbs.writes: new .ctr.jsonl + decl in the suite store
verbs.gate: span: sum(span.len)==source.len AND sha256(concat)==source.sha256. blob: CAS.get(blob_sha) returns the source bytes. PLUS determinism: converting twice yields a byte-identical file and an equal sha.

verbs.writes: opencode/OpenWork, via the CLOSED cowork_to_openwork boundary
verbs.gate: the ses_* id and workspace_id READ BACK from the live store. Recents assertion sits behind an availability probe, never a module-scope import (BLK-1).
proof JSON shaped like cow_migrator_rebind.json, plus the new workspace_id read back.
per-turn sha delta + n_turns delta. Identical sources => empty delta AND equal body_sha (only determinism makes this checkable).
typed VERIFIED / REFUSE(kind); for SEED, the precheck_seed result verbatim.
redactions > 0 on a fixture carrying a planted key; derived_from == parent sha; AND the parent's sha and mtime are unchanged - the proof the original stayed (R9).

verbs.writes: quarantine copy + new store; mutation only via rebind
verbs.gate: quarantine _MANIFEST.sha256.json, truncated_at_line, and a recovered n_turns BELOW the damaged store's claim. A recovery that reports no loss on a truncated store is a BUG, not a success.

gates: anonymize re-hashes the parent AFTER the run to prove the original was untouched.
crash-recover treats a loss-free recovery of a truncated store as a failure.
anti_placation_gates.why: Designed so a plausible 'it worked' cannot pass.

non_goals.statement: Not CORE kernel. Writes no ledger, no registry, no sched, no live/config, no live/state outside its own state/session_tools/ drop zone. check READS SEED; nothing writes it.
Does not rebuild Open Sessions or GET /api/v1/recents. That product is LIVE. The suite feeds the projection; the panel stays the display authority.
Does not re-ingest the 666, and does not re-run the 666 rebind - CLOSED. Both are CLOSED_VERB.
Does not recode cowork_to_openwork. migrate delegates to it as a closed boundary.
Legal transcripts stay omitted. legal:true heads carry no body from this profile.

Adds no clock and removes none. The suite is on-demand CLI. cosmos_own_clocks.py (13 logon tasks, cosmos_own_clocks.py:437-451) is untouched; no schtasks create and no schtasks /delete. A future scan clock is named here and deliberately NOT proposed.
Does not take Core :8770 down. No route added, no service restart, no port bound, no cosmos_service.py edit. The suite runs beside Core, not inside it.
Adds no writer. Nine verbs, one mutation point (rebind), zero new authorities.
